answer: A fable is easy to tell, so the ledger checks the trail instead. Each identity must anchor its vertex with two holders outside its own cluster, and one anchor serves one identity, so n aliases need n distinct anchors instead of one cooperative ring. Every anchor is priced by rank: the k-th anchor an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still requiring unrelated guarantors. A pulse audit replays a random vertex each epoch, and an unreplayed claim voids the whole structure and forfeits its stash, which cannot be pooled, lent or resold.
